item.title: Archistar
item.description:
Archistar addresses the slow, rule-heavy process of getting buildings approved. Its platform reads planning regulations and site data to show what can be built on a lot, such as height, setbacks, and density. Developers and architects can test ideas and see the potential of a site before they invest.

For design checking, the tool compares a proposed building against local codes and flags issues, which reduces the back and forth with planning authorities. Councils use it to review applications faster and with more consistency. Generative design features create massing options that fit the rules, and reports summarize feasibility.

item.title: DISCO
item.description:
DISCO helps legal teams handle the huge volumes of documents produced in lawsuits and investigations. Teams upload email, files, and chats, search and tag them, and decide what is relevant and privileged. The platform runs in the cloud, so reviewers can work together without managing servers.

AI features reduce manual review. Models rank documents by likely relevance, so reviewers see the important ones first, and generative tools summarize documents, answer questions about a set, and help build timelines. Law firms and corporate legal departments use it to cut review costs and speed up cases.

item.title: Mindtickle
item.description:
Mindtickle is a sales readiness platform. New hires follow structured learning paths with lessons and quizzes, and practice pitches by recording videos or role-playing with AI, receiving feedback. Managers review the practice and see how reps compare on skills.

The platform links training to results. It tracks which skills correlate with success, identifies gaps across a team, and connects with CRM data to see how readiness affects performance. AI features generate content, score practice sessions, and recommend coaching.

item.title: QuickBooks
item.description: QuickBooks is the accounting software most small businesses and their accountants know. QuickBooks Online runs in a browser and on phones, connects to bank accounts to import transactions, sends invoices, tracks bills and expenses, and produces profit and loss statements, balance sheets, and cash flow reports. It also supports sales tax tracking, inventory in higher tiers, and multi-user access for bookkeepers and accountants. A desktop edition remains for businesses that prefer installed software.

item.title: QuickNode
item.description:
QuickNode offers blockchain infrastructure as a service. Running a node for a blockchain takes hardware, storage, and maintenance, so QuickNode hosts them and gives developers endpoints they connect to over standard protocols. Apps use these endpoints to fetch balances, read smart contract data, and submit transactions.

Beyond basic access, the platform includes tools for data and automation. Add-ons offer token and NFT APIs, streaming of on-chain events, and workflows that move blockchain data into databases. It supports many networks, including Ethereum, Solana, and layer 2 chains, with dashboards for usage and performance monitoring.

item.title: Redis
item.description: Redis stores data in memory, which makes reading and writing it extremely fast. Developers use it as a cache that sits in front of a slower database, as a session store for logged-in users, as a message queue, and for leaderboards, rate limiting, and counters. Its data types, such as lists, sets, sorted sets, hashes, and streams, make these patterns easy to build with simple commands. It’s one of the most widely deployed pieces of infrastructure on the web.

item.title: Typesense
item.description:
Typesense is built for instant search experiences, like the results that appear as a user types in a store or documentation site. It keeps its index in memory for speed, handles typos by default, and supports filtering, faceting, sorting, and grouping. Its API is simple, and client libraries exist for popular languages.

It also supports modern retrieval needs. Vector search lets applications find results by meaning using embeddings, and hybrid search combines that with keyword matching. Built-in features can generate embeddings, and a conversational search mode answers questions using retrieved documents. Developers can run Typesense on their own servers or use Typesense Cloud.

item.title: Boundless
item.description:
Boundless helps people navigate US immigration paperwork. Users answer questions in a guided flow, and the software builds the forms needed for a case, such as a marriage-based green card or naturalization. Checks flag missing information and inconsistencies that often cause delays.

Human experts remain part of the process. Plans include review by immigration attorneys or specialists, and customers can get help with responding to requests from authorities. Tracking tools show deadlines and the status of the case, and educational material explains steps and timelines.

item.title: Canary Technologies
item.description:
Canary builds software for hotels. Guests can check in online before arrival, sign registration forms, verify identity, and pay deposits, which shortens lines at the front desk. After arrival, messaging lets them ask for towels, late checkout, or recommendations through text instead of calling.

An AI layer answers common questions and handles requests, routing issues to staff when needed. Upsell tools offer room upgrades and add-ons at the right moment, which brings extra revenue. Other products cover contactless payments, digital tipping, and a guest-facing digital tablet in rooms.

item.title: Collov AI
item.description:
Collov AI helps people imagine a space. A user uploads a photo of a room, picks a style such as modern, farmhouse, or minimalist, and the tool produces a redesigned image with furniture and decor. It can also virtually stage an empty room for real estate listings.

Interior designers use it to show clients options early, and real estate agents use it to make listings more appealing. Homeowners use it for ideas before buying furniture. The renders are visualizations and do not reflect exact measurements or the availability of products.

item.title: Datarock
item.description:
Datarock works in mineral exploration. Geologists take photos of drill core samples and log what they see, which is slow and subjective. Datarock’s models analyze the images to identify rock types, measure fractures, and capture structural features, producing consistent digital logs.

The faster, more objective data helps exploration teams make decisions about where to drill next and supports resource modeling. Results integrate with geological software, and the company has expanded to other imagery such as hyperspectral scans and borehole images.

item.title: Everlaw
item.description:
Everlaw helps legal teams work through evidence. Documents are uploaded, processed, and made searchable, and reviewers tag them, share notes, and build case narratives. Visual tools show relationships and timelines, and cloud delivery means teams can collaborate without installing software.

AI speeds up the work. Predictive coding ranks documents by likely relevance, clustering groups similar content, and generative features summarize documents, answer questions across a set, and draft deposition outlines. Everlaw has tools used by public interest lawyers and human rights investigators, and the company supports access programs.

item.title: Glass Health
item.description:
Glass Health helps with clinical reasoning and documentation. A clinician enters or dictates a patient summary, and the assistant proposes a list of possible diagnoses, along with reasoning and suggested next steps. A plan builder drafts assessment and plan sections, and reference citations let the user check where claims come from.

It also supports note writing, and a library of clinical guidelines and content supports decisions. Physicians, residents, and students use it to think through cases and save time on write-ups. The product emphasizes that the clinician stays responsible for decisions.

item.title: HiredScore
item.description:
HiredScore applies AI to the early stages of hiring. When applications arrive, it grades candidates against the requirements of the role, surfaces people who might be good fits, including past applicants and current employees, and helps recruiters focus on promising profiles first.

It integrates with applicant tracking systems and HR platforms, and Workday acquired the company to build AI into its talent products. Features include internal mobility recommendations, which help companies fill roles from within, and reporting to monitor process fairness and compliance.

item.title: Kentik
item.description:
Kentik gives network teams insight into how traffic moves. It collects flow records, routing information, and metrics from routers, switches, and cloud networks, stores them at large scale, and lets engineers query who is talking to whom and how much. That helps with capacity planning, troubleshooting, and cost control.

Security and reliability uses include detecting DDoS attacks and unusual traffic patterns, analyzing BGP routing changes, and finding the reason for a slowdown across multiple networks. An AI assistant lets users ask questions in plain language and speeds up root cause analysis. Cloud and data center networks are covered.

item.title: nCino
item.description:
nCino is cloud banking software. A bank uses it to manage the full lending process, from application to documents, analysis, approval, and closing, replacing paper and email chains. It covers commercial, consumer, and mortgage lending and account opening.

AI and automation reduce manual work. Models extract financial data from documents, assess credit risk, and flag items for review, and agents help with tasks like drafting credit memos. Dashboards give management visibility across the portfolio.

item.title: Quorum
item.description:
Quorum is a public affairs platform. Users track legislation and regulations, follow lawmakers, and keep a record of their outreach, all in one system. Alerts notify them when a bill moves or a hearing is scheduled, and a database of officials supports advocacy campaigns.

AI summarizes long bills, flags relevant provisions, and helps draft messages and reports. Constituent engagement tools let organizations mobilize supporters to contact officials. Teams use the data to plan strategy and measure impact.

item.title: Rogo
item.description:
Rogo focuses on the work of junior bankers and analysts, who spend hours digging through filings, transcripts, and data. A user asks a question in plain language, such as how a company’s margins compare with peers, and Rogo retrieves and analyzes the sources, citing where numbers came from.

It connects to financial data providers and a firm’s internal documents, produces outputs like comps and summaries, and fits into the workflow with tools such as Excel and PowerPoint. Security and compliance features suit regulated firms.

item.title: Seequent
item.description:
Seequent software helps geologists understand what lies underground. Its flagship Leapfrog creates 3D models from drill holes, geophysics, and maps, so teams can see ore bodies and structures, plan drilling, and estimate resources. Other products handle geotechnical data, groundwater, and geophysical modeling.

Mining companies, geotechnical engineers, and environmental consultants use these models for decisions. Cloud tools allow collaboration and centralized data management, and newer features apply machine learning to modeling tasks.

item.title: Shift Technology
item.description:
Shift Technology serves insurers. When a claim arrives, its models assess the likelihood of fraud, explain the red flags, and route the case, so investigators spend time on the suspicious ones while clean claims are paid quickly.

The company extends the approach to underwriting, subrogation, and customer service, and has added generative AI agents that help adjusters summarize files and handle routine tasks. Its customers include large carriers around the world.

item.title: Smartify
item.description:
Smartify is an app for cultural venues. A visitor opens it in a partner museum, scans an artwork with the camera, and the app identifies it and shows background, artist information, and audio commentary. Collections can be saved for later.

Museums use it to enrich visits without installing hardware, and to learn what visitors engage with. The platform includes tools for creating tours and for accessibility. Some partners are major institutions.

item.title: Free AI Face Swap
item.description:
Free AI Face Swap lets a user upload two photos and exchange the faces. The tool detects faces, aligns them, and blends the result. It runs in the browser, supports common image formats, and offers extra effects around face editing.

People use face swaps for entertainment, memes, and creative projects. The same technology can be misused to create misleading or non-consensual images, so use only photos of people who have agreed, and never use swaps to deceive or harass. Many places have laws about deepfakes and intimate image abuse.

item.title: BrowserStack Test Companion
item.description:
Test Companion is an AI agent for quality assurance. Instead of a separate dashboard, it works in the developer’s editor, where it can generate test scripts from a description or from the code, run them on BrowserStack’s device and browser cloud, and investigate failures.

Maintenance is a major use. Tests break when interfaces change, and fixing them takes time. The agent can update selectors, adjust steps, and rerun, which reduces the upkeep that makes automated testing costly. It works with common frameworks and connects to BrowserStack’s testing infrastructure.

item.title: Aixploria
item.description:
Aixploria collects AI tools in one searchable catalog. Visitors can browse by category such as writing, image generation, coding, video, and productivity, or filter by price type, and see short descriptions with links to the tools. Popularity rankings and lists of new additions help surface what is trending.

The site also publishes news and selections of the best tools for particular tasks. For someone trying to find a product for a specific need, a catalog like this saves time compared with searching the web. As with any directory, it reflects submissions and the editors’ choices, so entries vary in depth.

item.title: Dang.ai
item.description:
Dang.ai is a place to discover AI tools through community voting. Makers submit their products, users upvote them, and the top entries appear on the homepage. Categories cover writing, image, coding, video, and other areas, with each listing showing a short description and a link.

The model rewards recent launches, so it suits people who want to see what is new and popular. Voting can reflect marketing effort as much as quality, so rankings are a starting point. Comparing listings across several directories gives a better picture.

item.title: Nano Banana Pro
item.description:
Nano Banana is the name Google gave to its Gemini-based image model, and the Pro version targets higher quality. Users describe an image or edit a photo by instruction, such as changing the background or combining subjects, and the model produces a result that keeps people and objects consistent.

It is known for rendering legible text inside images, producing high-resolution output, and following detailed prompts, which makes it useful for posters, infographics, and product mockups. It is available in the Gemini app, through Google AI Studio and the API, and in other Google products.

item.title: Anomaly AI
item.description:
Anomaly AI is for people who work with data that is too big or messy for a normal spreadsheet. A user uploads Excel or CSV files or connects sources such as databases, warehouses, and Google Sheets, then asks questions in natural language. The tool answers with tables, charts, and written explanations.

The vendor emphasizes traceable answers, meaning the analysis is run as code against the data so results can be inspected and not just generated by a language model. It can merge files with database data in one analysis, find trends, and flag unusual values. A connector allows assistants like Claude to hand questions about your data to the service.

item.title: QuillBotAI Pro: Free AI Content Detector for Educators & Publishers
item.description:
QuillBotAI Pro offers a web tool where a user pastes text and receives a score estimating how likely it is to be machine written. It advertises detection of output from several major models, including text that has been rewritten to avoid detection, and positions the service as free and unlimited.

Educators and publishers use detectors as a first screen. Detection is inherently unreliable: tools produce false positives, especially on writing by non-native English speakers, and can miss edited AI text. A score should start a conversation, not decide a case.

item.title: Kaspr
item.description:
Kaspr is a contact data tool for outbound sales. While browsing a LinkedIn profile, a user clicks the Kaspr extension to reveal a professional email address and phone number, then saves the contact to a CRM or a list. It also supports bulk searches and enrichment of existing records.

The company emphasizes European data and compliance with privacy rules like GDPR, and offers ways for individuals to opt out of the database. Credits limit how many contact details a user can reveal each month, and integrations connect with CRMs and sales engagement tools.

item.title: Magic Patterns
item.description:
Magic Patterns turns an idea into a working interface. A user describes a screen or component, or uploads a screenshot or design, and the tool generates a React prototype that can be previewed and edited through chat or directly. It can follow a team’s design system so the result looks like the real product.

Designers and product managers use it to explore ideas and share clickable prototypes, and developers use it to get a head start on code. Features include collaboration, version history, and export to code or to Figma.

item.title: memoQ
item.description:
memoQ helps translators work faster and stay consistent. As a translator works through a document, the tool shows matches from a translation memory of earlier work and terms from a glossary, so repeated phrases are translated the same way. Machine translation can provide suggestions that the translator edits.

For teams, memoQ’s server and cloud products manage projects, assign work to translators and reviewers, and track deadlines and costs. It supports many file formats and quality checks, and integrates with machine translation engines and AI services, including large language models for suggestions and review.

item.title: Moonvalley
item.description:
Moonvalley builds generative video for creative professionals. Its Marey model is trained on licensed and rights-cleared footage, which the company positions as a safer choice for studios concerned about copyright. Users generate clips and have controls over camera movement, motion, and style.

Filmmakers use it to visualize scenes, build storyboards, and test ideas before expensive shoots, and agencies use it for concept work. The company works with filmmakers and studios, aiming at professional workflows more than casual social content.

item.title: Neon
item.description:
Neon rebuilt Postgres for the cloud by separating storage from compute. That design lets a database scale up under load and scale down to zero when idle, so you pay for use instead of keeping a server running. Developers get standard Postgres, which means existing tools, drivers, and extensions work, including pgvector for storing embeddings in AI applications.

The standout feature is branching. Because storage is copy-on-write, you can create a full copy of a database in seconds, like a Git branch, for testing a migration, running a preview environment for each pull request, or giving each developer an isolated copy. The same ability makes Neon attractive to AI coding agents and platforms that spin up many short-lived databases. Connection pooling, read replicas, and integrations with Vercel and other platforms are available.

item.title: PDF.ai
item.description:
PDF.ai lets people interact with documents. A user uploads a PDF, and an AI answers questions about it, with references to the pages where the answers appear. It can summarize chapters, pull out key points, and extract data.

It is used for papers, contracts, reports, and manuals, where reading everything is time consuming. Page citations let users verify answers, which matters because language models can misread or invent details.

PDF.ai has a free plan with limits and paid tiers. Sensitive documents deserve a check of the privacy policy. Alternatives include ChatPDF, NotebookLM, Humata, Claude and ChatGPT with file uploads, and AnythingLLM for local use. PDF.ai suits people who work with long PDFs.

item.title: Perplexity Pro
item.description:
Perplexity is an answer engine that searches the web and writes cited responses. The Pro tier raises limits on advanced searches and lets users choose among models, including Perplexity’s own and leading models from other labs, for harder questions.

Pro adds tools for research: upload and analyze documents, longer and more detailed searches, image generation, and access to deeper research modes that produce reports. Spaces let users organize topics and collaborate, and an API credit is sometimes included.

item.title: Planable
item.description:
Planable is built around approval workflows. Marketers create posts in a view that looks like the final social post, share it with teammates or clients, collect comments and approvals, and schedule it once signed off. This replaces long email chains and screenshots.

Features include a content calendar, multiple approval stages, and support for many networks. AI tools help draft captions and ideas. Agencies find it useful for client work where sign-off is required.

item.title: Prome AI
item.description:
Prome AI helps designers see concepts early. A user uploads a sketch, a screenshot of a 3D model, or a reference photo and writes a prompt, and the tool produces a realistic rendering with chosen materials, lighting, and style. This speeds up exploration before detailed modeling.

Architects use it for building massing and facades, interior designers for room concepts, and product designers for form studies. Variations can be generated quickly to compare options with clients.

item.title: GCS Cheats
item.description:
GCS Cheats sells subscriptions to cheat programs for multiplayer games, delivering license keys after payment. The tools advertised include aimbots, wallhacks that show enemy positions, and similar modifications that give a player an unfair advantage.

Using cheats breaks the rules of almost every online game and publisher, and anti-cheat systems detect and ban accounts, sometimes at the hardware level. Cheating also spoils the experience for other players. Software from cheat sellers can carry malware or steal account data, since it often needs to run with high system privileges, and buyers have little recourse if something goes wrong.

item.title: Exscientia
item.description:
Exscientia designed small-molecule drug candidates with AI models and ran automated labs to synthesize and test the top predictions. Results fed back into the models to improve the next round, a closed loop that aimed to shorten discovery time and reduce the number of compounds that must be made.

The company worked on cancer and other diseases, and formed partnerships with large pharmaceutical firms. It was among the first to move AI-designed molecules into clinical trials. After a period of strategic changes, it combined with Recursion, which brought together Recursion’s biology data and Exscientia’s chemistry design and automated synthesis.

item.title: Catchlight
item.description:
Catchlight is a lead scoring tool for financial advisory firms. It enriches a prospect’s profile with data such as estimated income, investable assets, age range, and interests, then applies a model trained on past conversions to produce a score showing how likely they are to become a client.

Advisors use it to prioritize their time. Instead of calling every inquiry, they can focus on those with the best fit, and see context to start a conversation. It integrates with CRMs used by advisors, such as Wealthbox, and appears in platforms that serve wealth management firms.

item.title: Relativity
item.description:
Relativity is a leading e-discovery platform. Legal teams load documents collected in a case, and the system processes them, makes them searchable, and lets reviewers tag and code them for relevance, privilege, and confidentiality. RelativityOne runs in the cloud.

AI helps lawyers cut review volume. Active learning ranks documents by likely relevance, clustering groups similar items, and generative features summarize documents and find key evidence. Analytics show patterns in communications, and audit trails support defensible processes.

item.title: Pulsara
item.description:
Pulsara speeds time-critical care. A paramedic starts a patient channel from the field, adds vitals and images, and alerts the receiving hospital, so teams can prepare before arrival. Stroke, heart attack, and trauma cases benefit when clinicians coordinate early.

Within the hospital, Pulsara links departments such as the emergency room, imaging, and specialists, and keeps a timeline of communications. The data supports review of response times and quality improvement. AI features assist with transcription and information routing.

item.title: Bambu Studio
item.description:
Bambu Studio turns 3D model files into instructions a printer can follow. You load a model, arrange it on the virtual build plate, set options such as layer height, supports, and infill, and the slicer generates the toolpath, previewing how the print will be built. It supports multicolor and multimaterial printing through Bambu’s automatic material system, with tools to assign colors and manage waste.

It is based on open-source slicer code and is itself open source. Features include automatic calibration, print profiles tuned for Bambu printers and common filaments, remote monitoring and control over the cloud, and integration with MakerWorld, Bambu’s online library of models, where users share designs and print profiles. It runs on Windows, macOS, and Linux and also supports some other printers.

item.title: Be My Eyes
item.description: Be My Eyes connects people who cannot see well with help. In the app, a blind or low-vision user can start a video call, and a sighted volunteer sees through the camera and helps with a task such as reading an expiry date, matching colors, finding a dropped item, or navigating an unfamiliar place. Millions of volunteers around the world have signed up, which means that help is usually available quickly, at any hour.

item.title: Buildxact
item.description:
Buildxact is built for builders who work from plans and spreadsheets and need a more organized way to price jobs. Users can create estimates from templates and cost catalogs, perform takeoffs from digital plans, and turn the estimate into a professional proposal. After a job is won, the same data feeds purchase orders, schedules, and cost tracking, so you can compare what you estimated with what you spent.

The software covers the flow of a residential project: estimating, quoting, selections, job scheduling, subcontractor coordination, and invoicing, with integrations to accounting software such as QuickBooks and Xero. AI features help read plans and speed up takeoffs, suggest items, and draft proposals. It targets small to mid-sized companies, such as custom home builders, remodelers, and specialty trades.

item.title: Crowdin
item.description:
Crowdin helps teams make products available in many languages. Developers connect their repositories, such as GitHub or GitLab, and Crowdin picks up new source strings, makes them available to translators, and syncs completed translations back, so localization keeps pace with development. It works with files from mobile, web, and game projects, and with content from design tools like Figma and from help centers.

The translation environment supports several workflows. Professional translators, in-house reviewers, and community volunteers can work in an editor with context, screenshots, glossaries, and translation memory that reuses past translations for consistency. Machine translation and AI features pre-translate content and suggest improvements, and quality checks catch errors. Project managers track progress and can order work from translation vendors through the platform.

item.title: Finch3D
item.description:
Finch3D addresses the early design stage, when architects test many layout ideas against requirements. You define a building footprint or site, along with rules such as unit mix, room sizes, and circulation, and Finch generates floor plan options that satisfy the constraints and optimizes them for factors like area efficiency. Architects can compare alternatives quickly instead of sketching each by hand.

The tool is built to fit architects’ workflows. It integrates with the design software they already use, including Revit, Rhino, and Grasshopper, so generated layouts can be refined and documented in familiar environments. It supports quick iterations when the brief changes, and provides metrics that help justify choices to clients, such as the number of units or usable area.

item.title: Geotab
item.description:
Geotab makes the small devices that plug into vehicles and report what they do. A device in the diagnostic port records location, speed, harsh braking, idling, engine fault codes, and more, and sends the data to the cloud, where fleet managers view it on maps and dashboards. Companies with delivery vans, service trucks, buses, and long-haul trucks use it to track vehicles, optimize routes, and reduce costs.

Analytics turn the data into insights. Driver scoring identifies risky behavior and supports coaching, maintenance alerts flag vehicles that need service based on engine data, and fuel and emissions reports support efficiency and electric vehicle planning. AI features include an assistant that answers questions about fleet data in natural language, and models that predict problems and rank safety risks. A marketplace of third-party apps extends the platform, and compliance tools support electronic logging rules.

item.title: Labelbox
item.description:
Labelbox helps AI teams turn raw data into labeled datasets. Its tools let annotators draw boxes and masks on images and video, tag text, transcribe audio, and rate model responses. Project management features assign work, review quality, and measure agreement between labelers, so teams can catch mistakes early. The platform supports both in-house labelers and external workforces.

The company has focused on generative AI. Tools support reinforcement learning from human feedback and model evaluation, where experts compare and rank responses, and a labeling service provides specialist annotators for domains such as coding, math, and medicine. Model-assisted labeling uses a model to pre-label data so humans only correct it, and data curation tools help find the most valuable examples. Integrations connect with cloud storage and ML pipelines.

item.title: Next Insurance
item.description:
NEXT Insurance focuses on small businesses such as contractors, consultants, cleaners, and shops. Instead of working with a broker, an owner answers a few questions online and gets a quote within minutes, buys the policy, and receives proof of insurance immediately. Digital certificates of insurance can be downloaded or sent to clients whenever needed, which saves time for tradespeople who must prove coverage to customers.

The company offers coverage lines such as general liability, professional liability, workers’ compensation, commercial auto, and tools and equipment. Its software uses data and automation to underwrite quickly and to handle policy changes and claims, with many tasks done in an app or on the website. The insurer is rated by industry agencies for financial strength.

item.title: TestFit
item.description:
TestFit speeds up the feasibility stage of real estate development. A user draws a site boundary and sets rules such as unit mix, parking ratios, setbacks, and building types, and TestFit generates layouts that fit, updating in real time as constraints change. It reports metrics like unit counts, parking, rentable area, and efficiency, which let developers judge whether a site works before investing heavily.

It handles multiple product types, including apartment buildings, townhomes, self-storage, hotels, and parking structures, and exports to common design tools such as Revit and CAD for the next stage. Cost and revenue features help assess returns, and collaboration tools let teams share scenarios. Generative algorithms explore many arrangements to find efficient solutions.

item.title: Testim
item.description:
Testim addresses one of the biggest pain points in test automation: tests that break whenever the interface changes. Instead of relying on a single brittle identifier for each element, it uses machine learning to learn multiple attributes of each element, so the test can still find a button after a developer renames or moves it. This self-healing behavior reduces the time engineers spend fixing tests.

Tests can be recorded by clicking through an app, then edited visually or with code for custom logic. The platform runs tests in the cloud across browsers and integrates with CI/CD tools, issue trackers, and test management systems, so test results fit into existing workflows. Features such as grouping and reusable steps help teams scale suites, and AI assists with test creation and failure analysis.

item.title: Tulip
item.description:
Tulip brings software to the factory floor. Engineers and operators build apps using a drag-and-drop editor, with steps that guide workers through assembly, inspection, or maintenance, collect data, and trigger actions. Connecting sensors, machines, and tools lets the apps read real-time values, and the platform replaces clipboards and spreadsheets with digital work instructions and quality checks.

Analytics and automation extend the value. Dashboards show production performance, quality, and downtime, and machine learning models can detect anomalies or predict issues. Generative AI helps create apps from a description and analyze data in plain language. As a lightweight manufacturing execution system, it can be adopted gradually, line by line.

item.title: Ultimaker Cura
item.description:
Cura converts 3D models into printer instructions. Users load a model, position it, choose a material and quality profile, and the software slices it into layers, with a preview that shows how the print will be built. Settings control supports, infill, speed, temperature, and more, and a simple mode hides complexity for beginners while a custom mode exposes hundreds of options.

It has a very large user base because it works with many printers, not only those made by UltiMaker. Community-maintained profiles cover popular brands, and a plugin marketplace adds features such as post-processing scripts and cloud integrations. Cura is developed in the open and has had long-running support from the maker community.

item.title: Vanta
item.description:
Vanta helps companies prove they run secure operations. It integrates with tools such as AWS, Google Workspace, GitHub, Okta, and HR systems, continuously checks whether controls like encryption, access reviews, and employee training are in place, and collects the evidence auditors need. This replaces manual screenshots and spreadsheets and keeps a company audit-ready year-round.

The platform has grown into a broader trust management suite. It tracks vendor risk, manages security policies and employee onboarding tasks, runs risk assessments, and provides a trust center where customers can see a company’s security posture. AI features answer security questionnaires, map controls across frameworks, and help prioritize remediation, saving time for small security teams.

item.title: Wealth.com
item.description:
Wealth.com brings estate planning into the advisory relationship. Advisors can generate estate documents for clients through guided workflows, with attorney review options, and offer a client portal that shows the plan visually. A vault stores documents.

AI reads existing estate documents and summarizes provisions, beneficiaries, and issues, which helps advisors understand a client’s situation quickly. The platform integrates with financial planning tools so estate information sits alongside the rest of the plan.

item.title: Weglot
item.description:
Weglot lets a site add languages without rebuilding it. You install a plugin or add a snippet, Weglot finds the text on your pages, translates it with machine translation, and creates versions of the site in the languages you choose. It also adds a language switcher and handles the technical parts of international SEO such as hreflang tags and translated URLs.

Quality control happens in a dashboard. You can edit any translation, use a glossary to keep brand terms the same, and order professional translations through partners for key pages. Translations are stored and reused, and visual editing lets you fix text in the context of the page. AI features improve consistency, and it works with many popular platforms.

item.title: XMind
item.description:
XMind is a long-standing mind mapping tool known for its range of layouts. Start with a central idea and branch outward, or switch to another structure such as a logic chart, fishbone diagram, matrix, tree chart, or timeline to fit the problem. It has a polished interface, attractive themes, and features such as markers, stickers, notes, and attachments, and it works offline.

Special modes help with presentation and organization. Brainstorming mode captures ideas quickly, outline view turns a map into a list, and Zen mode removes distractions. A presentation feature plays the map as a slideshow, and exports cover PDF, images, Word, and Markdown. AI features can generate a map from a topic, expand a branch with suggestions, and summarize content into a structure.

item.title: Adobe Lightroom AI
item.description:
Lightroom is built for photographers who handle many images. It organizes a library, lets you rate and filter, and edits photos non-destructively with sliders for exposure, color, tone, and detail. Edits can be copied across a whole shoot, which saves hours after a wedding or event. Lightroom syncs between desktop, phone, and the web, while Lightroom Classic is the desktop-only version with a more traditional file-based workflow.

AI has changed the way people edit in it. Masking tools select the subject, sky, background, or people with a click, so you can adjust one part of a photo without painting a selection. Denoise cleans up high-ISO images while preserving detail, Generative Remove deletes distractions, and Lens Blur adds realistic background blur. Adaptive presets adjust to the content of each photo, and auto-edit settings give a starting point.

item.title: Airtable
item.description: Airtable looks like a spreadsheet but behaves like a database. Records live in tables with typed fields such as dates, attachments, checkboxes, and links to records in other tables, which allows relationships that spreadsheets cannot handle. The same data can be shown as a grid, kanban board, calendar, gallery, or timeline, and filters and groups tailor each view. It’s used for content calendars, product roadmaps, CRM, event planning, and operations.

item.title: Altered AI
item.description:
Altered focuses on voice conversion, sometimes called speech-to-speech. You record a performance, and the system re-voices it in another voice from its library while keeping the timing, emotion, and delivery of the original. That differs from text-to-speech, where the machine invents the performance. For productions, it means one actor can voice several characters, or a performance can be changed to match a different character without a second recording session.

The tools are designed for professionals. Altered Studio provides a way to process recordings and fine-tune results, and the platform includes text-to-speech and voice cloning options for productions that need them. Typical customers are game studios, audiobook makers, animation and film teams, and agencies that localize content. Licensed voices matter in this field, since using someone’s voice without permission raises legal and ethical issues.

item.title: Amplitude AI
item.description: Amplitude helps product teams see what users actually do. You instrument your app or website to send events, such as signing up, clicking a button, or finishing a purchase, and Amplitude turns them into funnels, retention curves, user paths, and cohorts. These views answer questions like where new users drop off and which features bring people back. It is used by product managers, designers, and data analysts at companies from startups to large enterprises.

item.title: BambooHR
item.description:
BambooHR is built for companies without a large HR department. It keeps employee information in one place, tracks time off, handles onboarding checklists and documents, and offers an employee self-service portal. Applicant tracking helps with hiring, performance tools support reviews and goals, and payroll and benefits administration are available for U.S. customers. Reporting shows headcount, turnover, and other metrics.

The product is known for being easy to use, with a friendly interface and quick setup. AI features help HR teams with tasks such as drafting job descriptions and performance review language, summarizing feedback, and answering employee questions using company policies. Integrations connect with accounting, benefits, and productivity tools, and an app marketplace extends the platform.

item.title: BeFunky
item.description:
BeFunky is a browser-based editor for people who want quick results without learning Photoshop. The photo editor has sliders for exposure and color, crop and resize tools, and a large set of filters and effects. A collage maker arranges photos into layouts, and the graphic designer tool offers templates for social media posts, flyers, and cards. Everything runs in a web page, with mobile access too.

AI tools handle common edits. An enhancer sharpens and improves photos, a background remover cuts out subjects, and retouching tools smooth skin and remove blemishes. Artistic effects turn photos into paintings or cartoons, and an upscaler increases resolution. Newer features add AI image generation and a way to remove objects. Many of these are one-click operations, which is the main appeal.

item.title: Biteable
item.description:
Biteable makes video creation approachable for non-editors. Users pick a template for something like a company announcement, training clip, or social promo, and replace text, images, and footage scene by scene. Brand settings keep colors, fonts, and logos consistent across a team.

AI features accelerate the first draft. A script or prompt can generate a sequence of scenes with suggested visuals, text can be turned into narration, and videos can be resized for formats such as vertical social posts and widescreen. Collaboration features let teammates review and edit, and analytics show how videos perform.

item.title: Botkeeper
item.description:
Botkeeper offered accounting firms a way to scale bookkeeping with automation. Its software connected to clients’ accounting systems, categorized transactions with machine learning, reconciled accounts, and prepared financial statements, with human reviewers checking the work. The aim was to let firms serve more clients with the same staff and to reduce routine data entry.

The company raised substantial funding, but it shut down after losing a large share of its revenue when major customers were acquired and changed their arrangements. It then sold its Infinite AI platform to Xendoo, a bookkeeping firm, which said it would keep the platform active and supported as its own division. The long-term roadmap is less clear, and customers had to decide whether to move.

item.title: Clideo
item.description:
Clideo offers simple video tools that run in the browser. A user uploads a clip, picks a tool such as trimming, merging, compressing, resizing, or converting formats, and downloads the result. The pitch is convenience for quick jobs where installing editing software is not worth it.

AI features add some automation. Auto subtitles transcribe speech and add styled captions in many languages, and background removal and other effects help prepare clips for social media. The editor handles basic timeline work, and tools for audio, GIFs, and screen recording are included in the suite.

item.title: ContentStudio
item.description:
ContentStudio combines content discovery, creation, and publishing. Users find trending topics and articles, curate and share them, write posts with an AI assistant, and schedule to networks such as Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn, X, TikTok, and WordPress blogs. A calendar shows what is planned across channels.

Features for teams and agencies include approval workflows, client management, white-label reports, and analytics on performance. The AI writer generates captions, hashtags, and blog drafts, and image tools help create visuals. Social inbox features centralize replies and comments.

item.title: Copy.ai
item.description:
Copy.ai began as one of the first popular AI copywriting tools. Users choose a template or write a prompt, and the tool generates headlines, product descriptions, email sequences, ads, and social captions. A brand voice feature helps keep the tone consistent.

The product later shifted toward workflows for go-to-market teams. Marketers and sales teams can chain steps that research accounts, draft outreach, and produce content at scale, using multiple language models. Chat and knowledge features let the AI draw on company information.

item.title: Copy.ai
item.description:
Copy.ai started in the first wave of AI writing tools. You picked a template, such as a product description, email, or social caption, answered a few prompts, and got several drafts to edit. It was popular with marketers and small businesses who needed a lot of copy quickly. Over time it moved away from one-off text generation and toward automating sales and marketing processes.

Its later product centered on workflows. A team could chain steps together, for example researching an account, pulling in data, drafting outreach, and writing a CRM update, and let AI agents run the sequence on a schedule or trigger. A data layer called Tables kept the inputs organized, and the aim was to replace manual go-to-market busywork with repeatable automations rather than just generating paragraphs.

item.title: Craiyon
item.description:
Craiyon began as DALL-E mini, an open-source experiment that went viral for producing odd, low-resolution images from text prompts. It was one of the first image generators many people tried, and it popularized the idea that anyone could make pictures with words. The site then rebranded as Craiyon and kept its low barrier to entry: open the page, type a prompt, and wait for the results.

The quality has improved with newer models, and Craiyon now produces more detailed images in several styles, including photos, illustrations, and drawings. Paid plans remove ads, speed up generation, and add features such as faster queues, higher resolution, and a private mode. The tool is positioned for casual use, like quick illustrations, memes, and idea sketches, instead of professional production.

item.title: Expensify
item.description:
Expensify is known for making expense reports less painful. Employees photograph receipts or forward them by email, SmartScan extracts the merchant, date, and amount, and the app builds a report for submission. Managers approve in the app, and approved expenses sync to accounting software.

Other features cover company spending. The Expensify Card gives employees corporate cards with real-time receipts matching, policies flag out-of-bounds expenses automatically, and mileage tracking and per diems handle travel. AI helps categorize spending and spot policy issues.

item.title: FarmLogs
item.description:
FarmLogs began as a way for farmers to keep records digitally instead of in notebooks. Growers could map their fields, log planting, spraying, and harvest activities, track inputs and costs, and see weather and satellite imagery for each field. The aim was to make it easier to understand what was working in a season, to meet record-keeping requirements, and to share information with advisors and landlords.

The product became part of Bushel, a company that provides software for grain buyers, farmers, and the supply chain. Under the name Bushel Farm, it connects farmers with grain markets and elevators, shows contract and delivery information, and supports tools for tracking grain inventory. Data from fields and grain marketing is brought into one view, and analytics help evaluate profitability.

item.title: Fathom
item.description: Fathom is known for making meeting notes free. It joins your Zoom, Google Meet, or Microsoft Teams calls, records them, and creates a transcript in real time. You can highlight important moments during the call with a click, and within seconds of the meeting ending, it produces a summary with decisions, action items, and key points that you can share. The free plan includes unlimited recordings and transcripts, which set it apart from competitors that cap free use.

item.title: FlexClip
item.description:
FlexClip is a browser-based video maker for people without editing experience. You start from a template or a blank timeline, drop in clips, images, text, and music from its stock library, and trim and arrange them with drag and drop. It exports in common formats and sizes for social platforms, and includes screen and webcam recording for tutorials. It is used by small businesses, teachers, and social media managers.

AI features speed up production. Text-to-video builds a draft from a script or idea, an AI script writer drafts the narration, and auto subtitles transcribe speech and add captions in many languages. Background removal for video, text-to-speech voiceovers, and AI image generation fill other gaps. Some features turn a blog post or product page into a video, which marketers use for repurposing content.

item.title: Formula Bot
item.description:
Formula Bot is aimed at spreadsheet users who know what they want but not the syntax. You describe the calculation, such as finding the average of a column when another column equals a value, and it produces the formula with an explanation. It can also explain a formula you paste in and fix errors, which helps when you inherit a workbook full of nested functions.

The tool extends beyond formulas. It can write scripts, SQL queries, and regular expressions from descriptions, convert between formula dialects, and answer questions about data you upload by building charts and summaries. A chat-style data analysis feature lets users ask questions of a spreadsheet and receive results, aimed at people who don’t write formulas at all.

item.title: Gamma
item.description:
Gamma reimagined the presentation. Instead of slides built from a blank template, you describe what you want, such as a pitch for a new product or a lesson on photosynthesis, and Gamma generates a complete, designed deck with text, layouts, and images. The format uses flexible cards that expand and collapse, so presentations can feel more like interactive documents, and it also produces documents and one-page websites.

Editing is conversational and visual. You can ask the AI to rewrite a section, change the style, add images, or restructure, or edit manually with simple controls. Themes keep designs consistent, brand settings apply company fonts and colors, and sharing by link includes analytics on who viewed it. Decks can be exported to PowerPoint or PDF, and it integrates with other tools.

item.title: Gorgias
item.description:
Gorgias is a helpdesk made for online stores. Messages from email, live chat, social media, SMS, and phone arrive in one inbox, with the customer’s order history, shipping status, and account details shown next to the conversation. Agents can refund an order, edit an address, or cancel a shipment without leaving the ticket, which speeds up the most common support tasks in retail.

Automation takes care of a lot of the repetitive work. Rules route and tag tickets, macros fill in standard replies with order data, and self-service flows let shoppers track orders or request returns. An AI agent answers questions about shipping, returns, and products using the store’s policies and catalog, and can complete actions in the store before passing complex issues to people. Gorgias can also support sales conversations and product recommendations.

item.title: Greenhouse
item.description: Greenhouse is an applicant tracking system for companies that want hiring to be systematic instead of ad hoc. Each job has a defined process: a posting, a set of stages, interview kits with questions, and scorecards that interviewers fill out against the same criteria. The aim is to reduce bias and gut-feel decisions by making every candidate go through the same structured steps. Recruiters, hiring managers, and interviewers each get a view suited to their part of the work.

item.title: Hotjar AI
item.description:
Hotjar helps teams see what visitors actually do on a site. Heatmaps show where people click, move, and scroll, session recordings replay individual visits, and on-page surveys and feedback widgets ask visitors what they think. Together they reveal confusing layouts, broken elements, and places where people give up, which complements numbers from analytics tools that show what happened but not why.

AI cuts down the time it takes to find insights. Instead of watching hundreds of recordings, teams can get automatic summaries of sessions, highlights of common frustrations, and analysis of open-ended survey responses grouped into themes. This helps designers, product managers, and marketers decide what to fix first. Funnels and trends let you see where users drop out, and integrations send findings to tools like Slack, Jira, and HubSpot.

item.title: iNaturalist
item.description:
iNaturalist is a citizen science project and app. Users upload photos or sounds of organisms they find, a computer vision model suggests what species it is, and other observers weigh in. When enough people agree, the observation reaches research grade, and the data is shared with scientific databases.

The result is one of the largest collections of biodiversity observations. Researchers use it to track species ranges, detect invasive species, and study changes over time. Projects and bioblitz events organize community efforts, and schools use it for nature education.

item.title: Indeed
item.description:
Indeed started as a search engine for job listings, pulling postings from company career pages and other boards into one place. Job seekers search by title and location, set alerts, upload a resume, and apply directly, often in a few clicks. The site also provides salary estimates, company information, and reviews, and Indeed is now closely tied to Glassdoor, which is part of the same company.

For employers, it is a major source of applicants. Companies post jobs for free or pay to sponsor them for more visibility, and tools help with screening questions, scheduling interviews, and messaging candidates. AI features match job seekers to relevant roles and recommend candidates to employers, summarize job requirements, and increasingly assist with resume improvement and hiring workflows. Recruiters search a resume database, with paid access to some functions.

item.title: Kustomer AI
item.description:
Kustomer takes a CRM-style approach to support. Instead of treating each ticket as an isolated item, it builds a timeline for each customer that includes every conversation, order, and interaction across channels. Agents see the full history in one view, which reduces the need to ask customers to repeat themselves. Channels include email, chat, SMS, social messaging, and voice, and workflow rules automate routing and tagging.

AI features have grown in importance. AI agents can answer common questions, check order status, and complete simple actions, escalating complex cases to humans with context. Tools for human agents summarize long histories, suggest replies, and classify issues, and insights analyze conversation patterns to find problems in products or processes. The system connects with e-commerce and business platforms to bring in order and account data.

item.title: LANDR
item.description:
LANDR started with automated mastering. An artist uploads a mixed song, the system analyzes it, and an algorithm applies equalization, compression, and loudness adjustments, producing a master in minutes at a price below hiring an engineer. Style and loudness options guide the result.

The company now offers a wider set of services for independent musicians: distribution to streaming platforms, a marketplace of samples, plugins, a collaboration network, and tools for mixing and creating. A subscription bundles many of these.

item.title: Lexion
item.description:
Lexion helped legal teams make sense of their contracts. It read agreements, pulled out terms like parties, dates, renewal windows, and liability caps, and stored them in a searchable repository. Alerts warned teams about upcoming renewals and obligations, and workflows routed new requests.

AI answered questions across the portfolio, such as which contracts have auto-renewal or a particular clause. The company was built for fast-growing technology companies that wanted contract management without a heavy implementation.

item.title: Linear
item.description: Linear is a project management tool aimed at product and engineering teams. Its pitch is that the tool should get out of your way: pages load instantly, nearly everything can be done from the keyboard, and the data model is opinionated about how software gets built. Work is tracked as issues, grouped into cycles (time-boxed sprints), projects, and initiatives, with roadmaps on top for the longer view. Many teams switch to it from Jira because there is far less configuration to maintain.

item.title: Loom
item.description:
Loom replaces many meetings and long emails with a short video. You click record, show your screen while talking, and Loom uploads the video instantly and gives you a link to share. Viewers can watch at their own pace, react with emojis, comment at specific timestamps, and get an automatic transcript. It’s widely used for product walkthroughs, bug reports, onboarding, feedback, and updates to distributed teams.

AI features cut the work around videos. Loom creates titles and summaries, chapters for easy navigation, and action items, and can remove filler words and silences or turn a recording into a written document or ticket. Integrations connect with Slack, Jira, Notion, and Gmail, and since Atlassian acquired Loom, it fits more closely with tools like Jira and Confluence.

item.title: Mage.space
item.description:
Mage.space gives people a simple front end for open-source image models. You choose from a catalog of checkpoints, write a prompt, adjust settings like style, size, and number of images, and generate. It supports image-to-image transformations, inpainting, and control features that guide composition, and results can be upscaled. Because it hosts the models, users do not need a powerful computer or a local installation.

The platform appeals to people who want flexibility in styles, from realistic photos to anime and fantasy art, and who want to experiment with community-trained models. It has a gallery of public creations, and a text-to-video tool has been added to some plans. Content rules are looser than on some mainstream services, though it still prohibits illegal material.

item.title: MarketMan
item.description:
MarketMan is back-of-house software for food service. Operators record what they buy and use, build recipes with ingredient costs, and see the cost of each dish. When prices change or usage varies, the system flags it, helping managers protect margins.

Ordering and invoicing are handled in one place. Staff place orders with suppliers, receive deliveries, and match invoices to what arrived, which catches errors and short shipments. Forecasting tools predict how much to order based on sales history, and integrations connect with point of sale and accounting systems.

item.title: Maze
item.description:
Maze helps product teams learn from users. Designers import a prototype from Figma, set tasks for participants, and share a link to run a test that records clicks, paths, and success rates. Surveys, card sorts, and interview studies are supported as well, and a panel service can recruit participants.

AI speeds up analysis. It transcribes sessions, pulls out themes and quotes, and writes summaries of what the data shows, so teams spend less time sorting through recordings. Reports can be shared with stakeholders.

item.title: Mematic
item.description:
Mematic makes meme creation quick on a phone. Users pick a template from a large library or upload their own image, add captions in the classic style, and share to social networks and messaging apps. The interface is built for thumb use, so formatting text is fast.

The app offers sticker and filter options, categories of trending templates, and tools for adding emoji and shapes. A premium subscription removes ads and watermarks and adds more templates and features.

item.title: Mintlify
item.description:
Mintlify helps developer companies publish documentation that looks and works well. Teams write pages in MDX or Markdown, keep them in a Git repository, and Mintlify builds a fast, branded site with navigation, search, code samples, and API playgrounds generated from OpenAPI specs. Many well-known developer tools use it.

AI is part of both the reader and writer experience. An assistant on the docs site answers questions from the documentation, helping users find what they need, and docs are published in forms that AI coding tools can read, such as llms.txt and MCP servers. For writers, AI agents can draft pages, update docs when code changes, and flag outdated content. Analytics show what readers search for and where they get stuck.

item.title: Morningstar AI
item.description:
Morningstar is known for independent research on funds, stocks, and markets. Its star ratings for mutual funds and ETFs became a standard reference, and analysts publish research and fair value estimates on companies. Individual investors use its website and premium subscriptions to screen investments and build portfolios, while advisors and institutions use products like Morningstar Direct for deeper analysis, portfolio construction, and reporting.

AI has been added to make research easier to navigate. Mo is a conversational assistant that answers investing questions using Morningstar’s research and data, summarizes reports, and explains concepts, with an emphasis on drawing from the company’s own vetted content to limit errors. Other uses include automated summaries of earnings calls and analyst notes, and data tools that help build screens and analyze holdings.

item.title: Murf
item.description: Murf is known for its studio, but its voice features are a separate reason people use it. The voice changer converts a recording of your own speech into a different voice from the library, keeping your timing and emotion, which suits people who want a polished sound without hiring talent. Voice cloning can create a custom voice for a brand or presenter, typically with consent and verification, and is offered mainly for business customers.

item.title: Murf
item.description:
Murf is aimed at people who need a professional voiceover without hiring a voice actor or booking a studio. In its browser-based studio, you paste a script, choose a voice, and adjust pitch, speed, and emphasis. Voices come in many accents and languages and suit narration, e-learning, product videos, ads, and presentations. You can add background music, line the audio up with video or slides, and export the result.

The platform has expanded to related audio jobs. Dubbing translates a video or audio file into other languages and keeps it timed to the original. An API gives developers text-to-speech for their own apps, including fast, streaming voices for conversational use. Murf Agents power voice calls and chat for customer service and similar needs, and a voice changer converts one voice into another. Team workspaces help companies share projects and keep audio consistent.

item.title: Opendoor
item.description:
Opendoor popularized the iBuyer model. A homeowner enters an address and details, receives an offer within days based on the company’s pricing model and an inspection, and can close on a timeline they choose. The company then repairs and resells the home. The process appeals to sellers who value speed and certainty over getting the highest price.

Technology is central to the business. Machine learning models estimate what a home is worth and how long it will take to sell, using data on the property and the local market, and these estimates determine offers and risk. Opendoor also offers listing options for sellers who prefer to sell traditionally, along with buyer services such as touring homes with self-guided access in some markets.

item.title: OpenRead
item.description:
OpenRead is built for people who read a lot of research. After you import a paper, an AI assistant can answer questions about it, explain terms, summarize sections, and pull out items like methods, results, and limitations. A structured summary view lays out the main points in a consistent format, which helps when scanning many papers for a review.

The platform extends beyond a single paper. It helps search the literature, organize papers into collections, take notes alongside the text, and generate outlines or review drafts from selected sources. Support for multiple languages makes it useful for researchers who read in a second language, and translation features help with papers published in other languages.

item.title: Perplexity Pages
item.description:
Pages is a publishing layer on top of Perplexity’s research. After you explore a topic with the assistant, you can convert the thread into a structured page with headings, summaries, and citations to the sources it used. It organizes the material in the way a short article or study guide would be written, instead of leaving you with a conversation log.

You control the result. Sections can be rewritten, reordered, or removed, images can be added, and the page can be published with a shareable link or kept private. Educators use Pages to create study guides, students for report drafts, and professionals for quick explainers on topics they research often. Because the citations travel with the content, readers can check where claims came from.

item.title: Phind
item.description: Phind was built for programmers who had questions that a standard search engine handled poorly. A developer could ask how to fix an error, compare libraries, or write a function, and Phind searched the web and documentation, then wrote an answer with code snippets and links to its sources. It used its own coding-focused models and later offered an IDE extension and a chat interface for follow-up questions, and it was popular as a free alternative to general chatbots.

item.title: Pieces for Developers
item.description: Pieces helps developers avoid losing things they have already found. It runs a local service that captures and organizes code snippets, links, screenshots, and notes, enriches them with context such as where they came from, and makes them searchable. Plugins for VS Code, JetBrains, browsers, and other tools save snippets in a click and bring them back when you need them, so you don’t need to search again for how you solved something last month.

item.title: Pika Labs
item.description: Pika grew popular by making AI video fun and easy for people with no editing experience. You type a prompt or upload an image, and it generates a short clip in a few moments. Its signature features are effects that change objects in playful ways, such as melting, squishing, inflating, or turning something into cake, which spread quickly across social media. The interface is simple and mobile-friendly, which suited creators who make clips for TikTok and Instagram.

item.title: Pika Labs
item.description:
Pika makes short video easy. A user types a prompt, uploads an image, or provides a clip, and Pika generates or modifies footage. It is known for playful effects, like making objects melt or inflate, as well as realistic motion and camera control.

Creators use it for social posts, ads, and concept work. Features include editing parts of a video, extending clips, adding sound, and lip sync. The platform has expanded to support multiple underlying models and mobile apps.

item.title: Productivity Directory
item.description:
Productivity Directory collects tools that help people work better. Instead of listing every AI product, it focuses on productivity: task managers, calendars, note apps, automation, meeting assistants, and writing aids. Each listing has a short description, a category, and a link, so visitors can browse by need and compare similar tools quickly.

Directories like this serve people early in their search. A user who wants to improve how they plan their day or take meeting notes can see what exists and narrow down options before visiting individual sites. Editors choose which products to include, which gives it a more focused feel than massive catalogs, and new tools are added over time.

item.title: Proposify
item.description:
Proposify helps agencies and service companies create and send proposals. Teams build templates with sections, pricing tables, and brand styling, assemble a proposal quickly, and send it to clients who can review, comment, and sign electronically. Notifications show when a proposal is opened.

AI features help with writing content and suggest improvements based on what has worked in past proposals. Analytics reveal how long clients spend on each section, informing follow-ups. Integrations connect with CRMs and billing.

item.title: Replit
item.description:
Replit began as an online code editor and runtime that supported dozens of languages with no installation. Open a browser tab, start a project, and your code runs immediately on Replit’s servers. That made it popular in schools, coding bootcamps, and with beginners, and its multiplayer editing lets several people work in the same project at once. Projects are hosted, so sharing or deploying an app takes a click.

The current focus is Replit Agent, which builds software from natural language. You describe an app, and the agent writes code, sets up the environment, installs packages, creates a database, tests the result, and deploys it. You can keep chatting to refine features or fix bugs, or open the code and edit it directly. The aim is to let people without programming experience make working apps, and to let developers move faster. A mobile app lets you build and test from a phone.

item.title: ResearchRabbit
item.description:
ResearchRabbit helps researchers find papers they would not discover through keyword search. You add a few papers to a collection, and the tool suggests related earlier work, later work that cites them, and papers by connected authors, showing the connections in visual graphs. As you add more papers, recommendations get more specific, which makes it behave like a recommendation engine for research.

Collections keep projects organized, and alerts notify you when new papers match your interests. You can see networks of authors, explore how a field evolved, and export references to managers like Zotero. It is popular with students and academics who are starting a literature review or entering a new topic, and who want something more exploratory than a search box.

item.title: Resume.io
item.description:
Resume.io helps job seekers create a polished resume quickly. You choose a template, fill in your experience, education, and skills in a guided form, and see the layout update. The templates are designed to be clean and readable by applicant tracking systems, and you can adjust colors and fonts, reorder sections, and download the result as a PDF. Cover letter and CV builders follow the same approach.

AI features help with the hard part, which is the wording. The assistant suggests bullet points for a job title, drafts a professional summary, and can tailor a resume to a job description. A resume checker highlights weaknesses, and a job tracker helps manage applications. The tool also provides guides and examples for different professions.

item.title: Rev
item.description:
Rev started as a human transcription marketplace and added automatic transcription as speech recognition improved. Users upload audio or video, and receive a transcript within minutes from the AI service, or within hours from human transcribers who deliver higher accuracy. The choice lets you trade cost and speed for precision, which matters for legal proceedings, journalism, and broadcast captions.

Beyond transcripts, Rev offers captions and subtitles in many languages, translation, and a web editor for correcting and exporting text. Meeting tools record calls and produce notes, and an API supports developers who want to add transcription to products. Accessibility compliance is a big use, because captions help meet legal requirements for education and media.

item.title: Rosetta Stone
item.description: Rosetta Stone teaches by immersion. Instead of translating from your own language, lessons pair images with words and phrases in the target language, so you learn by association, the way children pick up a first language. Lessons build from simple vocabulary to conversation, with exercises on listening, reading, writing, and speaking. It has been a recognized name in language learning for decades and sells courses in about two dozen languages.

item.title: Runway Gen-3
item.description:
Gen-3 Alpha improved on earlier versions with finer detail, better handling of motion, and more consistent results across frames. Users could generate clips of several seconds from a prompt, an image, or both, with controls for camera movement and style.

It was trained on both images and video, aiming to understand how things move, and supported features such as image-to-video and video-to-video. Filmmakers and agencies used it for concept work, ads, and visual effects experiments.

item.title: Smartcat
item.description:
Smartcat brings machine and human translation together. A company uploads documents or connects content sources, receives AI translation immediately, and can request human review from freelance linguists or agencies in its marketplace, all with translation memory and glossaries.

Workflow tools manage projects, deadlines, and payments, and the platform supports many file types and integrations. AI agents handle tasks such as quality checks, and the pricing model aims to keep costs lower than traditional agencies.

item.title: Smartly.io
item.description:
Smartly, formerly Smartly.io, serves brands and agencies that run large ad programs. Its platform connects to major social networks and lets teams build and launch many campaigns from one interface, apply rules, and update thousands of ads at once. For retailers with big catalogs, dynamic ads are generated automatically from product feeds, adjusting to inventory and price.

The product emphasizes creative and optimization. Creative automation produces many ad variations in different sizes and languages from templates, which helps with testing and localization. Predictive budget allocation shifts spend among campaigns based on performance, and reporting brings results across platforms together. Newer generative features help create and adapt creative assets, with brand controls.

item.title: Speechify
item.description: Speechify turns reading into listening. You import text from the web, a PDF, an email, or a photo of a page, and the app reads it aloud at the speed you choose, highlighting the words as it goes. That makes it useful for catching up on articles while commuting, for studying, and for people with dyslexia or other reading differences, who often find audio easier to process. Apps for iOS, Android, Chrome, and the web sync your library.

item.title: Superhuman
item.description:
Superhuman became known as the fastest email client. It’s designed so you can process your inbox with the keyboard, using commands for archiving, replying, snoozing, and reminders, and everything loads instantly. The interface is minimal, with Split Inbox sections that separate important mail from newsletters and notifications. Features such as send later, follow-up reminders, read statuses, and a command palette are built into the workflow.

AI is now part of the experience. It drafts replies in your voice, summarizes long threads, searches your mail in plain language, and can write emails from short prompts. The company that owns Superhuman acquired it, changed its own name to Superhuman, and groups it with Grammarly’s writing assistant and the Coda workspace in a combined suite.

item.title: Vercel AI
item.description:
Vercel makes deploying web applications simple. Developers connect a repository, and every push builds and deploys to a global network, with preview URLs for each change. It is the home of Next.js and used by many teams for sites and apps.

For AI, Vercel provides the AI SDK, which standardizes streaming, tool calling, and structured output across model providers, plus an AI Gateway for routing requests and tracking cost. Its v0 tool generates interfaces from prompts, and agents and sandboxes support more advanced workflows.

item.title: Whimsical AI
item.description:
Whimsical puts several lightweight visual tools in one place. You can draw flowcharts and sequence diagrams, sketch low-fidelity wireframes, brainstorm on mind maps, write docs, and arrange sticky notes on a board. The tools are designed around speed, with keyboard shortcuts, snapping, and a clean look that makes rough thinking easy to share.

AI features reduce the setup. Describe a process and Whimsical can draft a flowchart, turn a topic into a mind map, or produce a first-pass wireframe, which you then edit by hand. Teams use it for planning, product specs, and explaining systems, and sharing is simple with links, comments, and embeds in tools like Notion and Confluence.

item.title: Wix ADI
item.description:
Wix ADI, short for Artificial Design Intelligence, was an early attempt at automatic site building. A user answered questions about their business and style, and ADI generated a layout with text, images, and a structure suited to the industry.
