It let people with no design skills get a website online in minutes, long before generative AI was common.

ADI sites had limits. They used a simpler editor than the main Wix Editor, which made it hard to customize them or to add advanced features. Wix has since retired the product: ADI sites are no longer supported and existing ones were moved into the standard Wix Editor, so owners can keep editing them there.

item.title: Zest AI
item.description:
Zest AI helps lenders approve more borrowers safely. Its models use many variables to estimate credit risk, aiming to include people thin credit files would exclude while keeping losses in check. Lenders deploy the models in their own decisioning workflows.

Explainability is central, since regulators require lenders to give reasons for adverse decisions. Zest provides tools to explain scores and to test models for disparate impact across groups. Credit unions and community banks are among its customers.

item.title: Zety
item.description: Zety walks job seekers through making a resume. You choose a template, answer prompts about your experience and education, and see a preview that updates as you type. The builder suggests wording for job duties and skills, which is helpful if you struggle with the phrasing, and it formats everything cleanly for PDF or Word download. It also builds cover letters and offers a library of guides and examples for different industries.

item.title: Zillow
item.description:
Zillow is where many people begin looking for a home. Listings for sale and rent appear on maps and lists with photos, price history, taxes, and school details, and users can filter by price, size, and features, save searches, and get alerts when matching homes appear. Agents and landlords pay to advertise or manage listings.

Its signature feature is the Zestimate, an automated estimate of a home’s value based on public records, market data, and a machine learning model. It is useful as a rough guide but can be off for individual homes, and sellers should not treat it as an appraisal. Zillow also offers mortgage and agent referral services, rental tools, and an AI-powered search that accepts natural language descriptions.

item.title: ZipRecruiter
item.description:
ZipRecruiter works on both sides of hiring. An employer writes a job once, and ZipRecruiter posts it across a network of job boards and sends it to potential candidates through email and notifications. Job seekers create a profile or upload a resume, browse listings, set alerts, and apply with a click, and the platform recommends jobs based on their interests and activity.

Matching technology is central. The system learns from employer and candidate behavior to recommend candidates to employers and jobs to seekers, and employers can invite candidates to apply. Tools help screen applicants, schedule interviews, and communicate in one place. AI features assist with writing job descriptions and surfacing strong matches, and an employer dashboard tracks responses.

item.title: Animoto
item.description:
Animoto was built for people who need a video quickly and do not know editing software. A user uploads photos and video clips, picks a template and a song, and the tool arranges them into a polished video with text and transitions. A storyboard view lets you rearrange scenes and change styles.

It aims at small businesses, real estate agents, educators, and social media marketers. Templates fit common formats such as promos, slideshows, and testimonials, and brand tools apply logos and colors. Videos can be shared online or exported for ads and websites. Newer AI features speed up layout and text creation.

item.title: Close
item.description:
Close takes the position that sales reps should do their work from one screen. Calls, emails, and texts happen inside the CRM and are logged automatically, so there is less manual data entry and a complete history on each lead. Power dialers let reps work through lists quickly.

Sequences automate multi-step outreach that mixes email, calls, and texts, and workflows keep pipelines moving. AI features transcribe and summarize calls, suggest follow-ups, and score leads, which helps managers coach and helps reps decide where to spend time. Reporting shows activity and results by rep.

item.title: Codecademy
item.description:
Codecademy teaches coding by doing. Lessons present a short explanation beside an editor where learners write code and see results right away, which makes it approachable for beginners. Courses cover languages such as Python, JavaScript, and SQL, as well as web development, data analysis, and machine learning.

Career paths and skill paths structure the learning, with projects and quizzes to check progress. An AI assistant helps learners who are stuck by giving hints and explaining errors, while avoiding simply handing over answers. Business plans let companies train teams, and Skillsoft acquired Codecademy to add it to its corporate learning catalog.

item.title: Copysmith
item.description:
Copysmith targets online retailers that need lots of product copy. A merchant can generate descriptions for many products from a spreadsheet or catalog, create ad headlines and text, and draft emails and social posts. Bulk generation saves time when a store has hundreds of items.

Integrations connect it to Shopify and Google Ads, so content can flow into the tools where it is used. Team features allow collaboration and approval, and brand settings keep tone consistent. Some tools support SEO optimization by suggesting keywords.

item.title: Freshsales
item.description:
Freshsales is a sales CRM that keeps lead and deal information in one view. Teams track contacts, run pipelines, and log calls and emails, with a built-in phone and chat so reps can contact prospects without switching tools. Automation moves leads through stages and assigns tasks.

Freddy AI assists with prioritization. It scores leads by likelihood to convert, predicts which deals will close, and suggests next best actions, while generative features draft emails and summarize conversations. Analytics show pipeline health, and integrations connect with Freshdesk, marketing tools, and common business apps.

item.title: Front
item.description:
Front treats shared inboxes like collaborative workspaces. Support, sales, and account teams manage messages from several channels in one place, assign conversations, leave internal comments, and see who is handling what. The interface resembles email, so adoption is easy.

Automation and AI reduce manual work. Rules route messages, tag them, and set priorities, while AI summarizes long threads, suggests replies, and answers common questions. Analytics show response times and workloads, and integrations with CRMs and helpdesk tools provide context.

item.title: Gladia
item.description:
Gladia provides speech-to-text as a service for developers. Companies send audio from calls, meetings, or videos and receive transcripts with timestamps, speaker labels, and optional translation. It handles dozens of languages and can detect which one is being spoken.

Real-time transcription suits live captioning and voice agents, while batch processing handles recordings at scale. Extra features include summaries, sentiment, and named entity detection. The API is aimed at products built on audio, such as meeting assistants, call analytics, and media tools.

item.title: Guru
item.description:
Guru stores verified knowledge in cards that teams can find where they work. A browser extension and Slack integration surface relevant answers without leaving the page, and experts verify cards on a schedule so that the information stays trustworthy. The idea is a single source of truth for sales, support, and internal teams.

AI search connects to the company’s other sources, such as documents, chat, and ticketing systems, and answers questions in natural language with citations. Analytics show what people search for and which content is stale. Admins control who can see what, and the AI respects those permissions.

item.title: Jammable
item.description:
Jammable, formerly Voicify, lets people hear songs sung in a different voice. A user chooses a voice model from a library, uploads a vocal or song, and the system converts it so it sounds like the chosen voice. Fans and creators use it for parodies, mashups, and experiments.

The technology raises serious legal and ethical issues. Voices of real artists are protected in many places, and music labels and artists have objected to unauthorized voice clones. Sharing such covers can violate copyright and rights of publicity, and platforms may remove them. Use voices you have permission to use, and avoid presenting synthetic songs as the real artist.

item.title: Lever
item.description:
Lever pairs two things that recruiting teams often keep separate: an applicant tracking system for people who apply, and a relationship manager for people you want to attract. In one place, recruiters post jobs, move candidates through stages, schedule interviews, collect feedback, and build talent pools for roles that open later. The pipeline view is visual and quick to scan, which suits teams that hire continuously.

Sourcing and nurture are a focus. Lever can run email sequences to passive candidates, track responses, and bring prospects into the same pipeline as applicants. Interview scheduling is automated so recruiters spend less time on calendars, and scorecards keep feedback structured. Reporting covers the funnel, diversity data, and time to hire. Integrations link it to job boards, HR systems, and assessment tools.

item.title: Neon
item.description:
Neon runs PostgreSQL in the cloud with a design that lets databases scale to zero when idle and start quickly when needed. Because storage and compute are separate, it can create copy-on-write branches of a database instantly, which suits testing, previews, and development workflows.

Branching has become useful for AI work, where agents and coding tools create databases on the fly. The pgvector extension supports embeddings and similarity search, so developers can store vectors next to ordinary data. The platform is used with frameworks like Next.js and with serverless hosts.

item.title: Pallyy
item.description:
Pallyy keeps social management simple and affordable. Users connect accounts, plan posts on a visual calendar, and publish to several networks. A first-comment feature, link-in-bio pages, and a media library support common creator workflows, and a unified inbox collects comments and messages.

Analytics show growth and engagement, and client-friendly reports help agencies prove results. Collaboration tools let clients approve content before it goes live. AI features suggest captions, hashtags, and ideas to speed up planning.

item.title: Remesh
item.description:
Remesh scales the focus group. A moderator poses questions to hundreds of participants at once, and people respond in their own words and then rate each other’s answers, so the group quickly reveals where opinions agree and differ. Responses are analyzed as they arrive.

AI clusters comments into themes, summarizes sentiment, and highlights segments by demographic. Researchers use it for message testing, employee listening, public policy input, and product research. A single session can produce depth and breadth that would take many interviews.

item.title: Revenue.io
item.description:
Revenue.io, formerly RingDNA, combines calling with conversation intelligence. During a call, it listens and surfaces prompts, such as a competitor battlecard or the right answer to a pricing objection. After the call, it transcribes, summarizes, and scores conversations against a playbook.

Managers get coaching insights and forecasting signals. The platform includes a dialer and integrates with Salesforce, so call data flows into the CRM. AI assistants draft follow-ups and update records.

item.title: Spike
item.description:
Spike presents email like a chat. Threads become conversations, which can feel faster, and a unified view combines email with notes, tasks, and calendar. Teams can discuss messages privately without forwarding.

AI helps with summaries of long threads, drafting replies, and organizing the inbox, and shared inboxes support small teams. It works with many email providers.

Spike has a free tier and paid plans. Chat-style email is a taste, and some prefer traditional layouts. Alternatives include Superhuman, Shortwave, Hey, Gmail with Gemini, and Front. Spike suits people who want a conversational inbox.

item.title: Submagic
item.description:
Submagic speeds up editing of talking-head clips. A creator uploads a video, the tool transcribes speech, adds styled captions that highlight words as they are spoken, and suggests emojis, sound effects, and B-roll to keep viewers engaged.

Templates provide the caption looks seen on popular social videos, and users can edit text, timing, and style. Tools for trimming silence and magic clips from longer videos add to the toolkit. Multiple languages are supported.

item.title: Turbopuffer
item.description:
Turbopuffer rethinks vector database economics. Instead of keeping all data in expensive memory, it stores vectors in cheap object storage and caches the hot data, which keeps costs low for large collections while keeping latency low for frequently used data.

It supports full-text and vector search with filters, and serverless pricing means no clusters to manage. Companies use it for retrieval in AI applications that have very large corpora.

Turbopuffer is usage-priced. Query latency on cold data is higher than on cached data. Alternatives include Pinecone, Qdrant, Milvus, Weaviate, and pgvector. Turbopuffer suits teams storing very large vector collections.

item.title: Viz.ai
item.description:
Viz.ai is known for its stroke software. When a patient has a CT scan that may show a large vessel occlusion, a blockage in a major brain artery, the AI analyzes the images within minutes and alerts the stroke team on their phones, with images they can view immediately. Speeding up that notification can cut the time to treatment, which matters in stroke, where each minute affects outcomes.

The platform has expanded beyond stroke. It supports other conditions, including pulmonary embolism, aortic disease, and heart conditions, and uses AI to identify patients who may be eligible for treatment or follow-up. A care coordination layer links hospitals, so specialists at a distance can review cases, communicate, and arrange transfers. Several of its algorithms have received regulatory clearance in the United States.

item.title: Adobe Acrobat AI
item.description: Acrobat AI Assistant adds a chat panel to the PDF reader most offices already use. Open a contract, report, or research paper, and you can ask for a summary, a list of action items, or an answer to a specific question. Each answer links back to the passage it came from, which makes it practical to check the work instead of trusting it blindly. It handles long files that would take an hour to skim.

item.title: AIWriteBook
item.description:
AIWriteBook is aimed at people who want to produce a book without doing every step by hand. The workflow starts with a topic, generates an outline, drafts chapters, and offers editing passes. Extras include cover design and formatting for publishing platforms such as Amazon KDP.

Tools like this attract self-publishers, especially in nonfiction niches. They also raise concerns. Books produced mostly by AI can lack depth, accuracy, and a personal voice, and readers and platforms are wary of low-effort content. Amazon requires authors to disclose AI-generated content when publishing, and quality problems lead to poor reviews.

item.title: Automateed
item.description:
Automateed focuses on turning an idea into a finished ebook quickly. A user enters a topic or outline, the tool drafts chapters, and the author edits and arranges them. The platform then handles formatting and export in common ebook formats, with covers and other publishing steps in the workflow.

The audience is self-publishers and marketers who produce lead magnets, guides, and short nonfiction books. The convenience comes with tradeoffs. Mostly machine-written books can be generic, may contain factual errors, and face skepticism from readers and retail platforms. Amazon asks authors to disclose AI-generated content when publishing.

item.title: biela.dev
item.description:
Biela.dev belongs to the group of prompt-to-app tools. A user describes the product they want, and the platform generates the code for the interface and logic, previews it in the browser, and lets the user request changes in conversation. When satisfied, they can deploy it online.

These tools suit prototypes, internal utilities, and early product tests. They shorten the path from idea to something clickable, which helps founders show investors or customers what they have in mind. Generated code can be exported for developers to continue.

item.title: ClipDrop
item.description:
Clipdrop packages common image edits into simple web tools. Remove Background cuts out a subject in a click, Cleanup erases unwanted objects, Image Upscaler enlarges small pictures with added detail, and Uncrop extends an image beyond its borders. Relight changes the lighting on a subject, and Replace Background swaps in a new scene from a text prompt. A text-to-image generator rounds out the set, using Stability AI models.

Product photographers, e-commerce sellers, marketers, and casual users reach for it when they need a quick edit without opening a heavy editor. The tools work in the browser and on mobile, with an API for developers who want to add the same features to their own apps. The project had a short stint under Stability AI before moving to Jasper, which acquired it to expand its marketing tools.

item.title: Connected Papers
item.description: Connected Papers helps you get oriented in a research area. You enter a paper title, DOI, or link, and it produces a graph where each node is a paper and closer nodes are more similar. Similarity comes from co-citation and bibliographic coupling, meaning papers that cite similar sources or are cited together, rather than from keywords. Node size and color show citation count and year, which lets you see influential and recent work at a glance.

item.title: Drift
item.description: Drift popularized the idea of replacing a website contact form with a live conversation. A chat widget greets visitors, asks a few questions, and either answers them, routes them to the right salesperson, or books a meeting on the spot. For B2B companies with long sales cycles, the goal was to catch interested visitors while they were still on the site instead of waiting for them to fill out a form and wait for a reply.

item.title: EchoWrite
item.description:
EchoWrite aims to make dictation work everywhere on a Windows PC. A user presses a hotkey, speaks, and the text appears in the active application, such as a word processor, email client, or code editor. AI cleans up punctuation and filler words so the result reads closer to written text.

Voice typing is faster than typing for many people, and helps those with repetitive strain issues. Accuracy depends on the microphone, accent, and vocabulary, and a quiet environment helps. Specialized terms may need custom dictionaries.

item.title: Eightfold AI
item.description:
Eightfold AI treats talent as a graph of skills. Its models read resumes, job descriptions, and employee profiles, infer skills, and match people to roles based on what they can do and are likely to learn, not just on keywords or job titles. Recruiters use it to find candidates in a company’s applicant database and external sources, and employees can see roles and learning paths that fit their skills.

The platform extends across the employee lifecycle. Modules cover talent acquisition, talent management, internal mobility, and workforce planning, with analytics that show skill gaps and diversity trends. Agent-style features automate steps such as screening and scheduling. It integrates with applicant tracking and HR systems such as Workday and SAP SuccessFactors.

item.title: FastBots
item.description:
FastBots lets small businesses add a chatbot without developers. A user points the platform at their website, uploads files, or adds frequently asked questions, and it builds a bot that answers customers using that content. The bot is embedded with a snippet of code or connected to channels such as messaging apps.

Additional features include lead capture, handoff to a human, conversation history, and analytics on what visitors ask. Customization options control the look, tone, and behavior of the bot, and integrations send data to other tools. It is positioned as a quick setup for support and sales questions.

item.title: Haiper
item.description:
Haiper launched as a fast, accessible video generator. Users typed a prompt or uploaded an image and received a short clip, with tools to extend videos, repaint areas, and animate stills. The company emphasized speed and iteration, aiming to let creators try many ideas quickly, and attracted attention as one of the more promising independent challengers to larger video model makers.

It could not keep pace with the rapid advances and heavy computing costs of video models. The company closed its consumer platform, and its founders moved to other roles, while its video models were acquired by another company that offers them through an API for enterprises. User projects hosted on the original platform were no longer accessible.

item.title: HireVue
item.description:
HireVue lets candidates complete interviews on their own schedule. Employers set up structured questions, candidates record video answers, and recruiters review them later, which saves scheduling time when hiring many people. The platform has expanded to include game-based and skills assessments, live interviews, text-based chat for scheduling and screening, and tools for coding interviews.

Its use of AI has been controversial. HireVue once analyzed facial expressions and voice in interviews, which drew criticism from privacy and civil rights groups, and it dropped facial analysis. Today it describes using structured scoring based on what candidates say and on job-relevant skills, and publishes audits and explanations of its models. Regulations in places such as New York City and Illinois now require notice, consent, or bias audits for automated hiring tools.

item.title: HumanizerFree.com
item.description:
HumanizerFree takes text produced by an AI model and rewrites it with varied phrasing, sentence length, and word choices so it reads less like machine output. A user pastes text, runs the tool, and edits the result. The tool is free for basic use.

Such tools raise questions. Using them to hide AI use in contexts where it is prohibited, such as some schoolwork, may break rules and can count as academic dishonesty. AI detectors are unreliable, so humanizers do not guarantee any result, and a rewrite can introduce errors or awkward phrasing.

item.title: Lovable
item.description: Lovable lets people describe an app and get something that runs. You type what you want, such as a task tracker, a booking tool, or a customer portal, and it generates a React front end, sets up pages and components, and shows a live preview. You then keep chatting to change the layout, add features, or fix problems. It is popular with founders, designers, and product managers who want a prototype without a development team.

item.title: MagicSlides
item.description:
MagicSlides speeds up deck creation. A user enters a topic, pastes text, or uploads a document, and the tool builds slides with titles, bullets, and images. Because it works as an add-on inside Google Slides and PowerPoint, the results land in a familiar editor for refinement.

It supports many languages and offers themes and layouts. Students use it for assignments, and professionals use it to produce a first draft of a presentation, which they then edit. Images can be sourced automatically.

item.title: Photoroom
item.description:
Photoroom grew from a background remover into a full product photography tool. Take a picture of a product on a table, and the app cuts it out cleanly, then places it on a white background, a color, or an AI-generated scene with realistic shadows and lighting. For small sellers on marketplaces like Etsy, eBay, and Shopify, that means professional-looking listings without a studio.

Other features expand the range. An AI backgrounds tool creates settings from a text description, an instant shadow and relight tool adds depth, and a magic retouch removes objects and blemishes. Templates in standard sizes speed up posts for social media and marketplaces. Batch editing handles whole catalogs, and an API lets platforms add the same processing to their own apps. Teams can share brand templates.

item.title: Pixlr
item.description:
Pixlr offers editing in a browser without installing software. Pixlr E is a more advanced editor with layers, masks, and adjustment tools that resemble Photoshop, while Pixlr X is a simpler editor for quick fixes, collages, and templates. It opens common image formats, including PSD files to an extent, and works on desktop and mobile browsers.

AI features handle the hard parts. Background removal makes cutouts in a click, an object eraser removes distractions, generative fill and expand add or extend content from a prompt, and automatic enhancement and retouching improve photos. An AI image generator and tools for creating designs from templates broaden what it can do. Pixlr is part of the Inmagine group, which also offers stock content.

item.title: Ramp
item.description:
Ramp issues corporate cards and wraps them in software for controlling spending. Companies give employees physical and virtual cards with limits and rules, and receipts are captured and matched automatically through the app. Finance teams see spending in real time and avoid chasing employees for expense reports. Ramp is known for fast growth among startups and mid-sized businesses.

The product has widened into a finance operating system. Bill pay handles vendor invoices, procurement tools manage purchase requests and approvals, and accounting automation categorizes transactions and syncs with systems such as NetSuite, QuickBooks, and Xero. AI agents review expenses against policy, suggest ways to cut costs from vendor spending data, and handle routine tasks such as coding transactions and preparing month-end close.

item.title: Recall
item.description:
Recall acts as a personal archive that organizes itself. A user saves a web page, YouTube video, podcast, or document with a browser extension or app, and Recall produces a summary, extracts key points, and links the item to related content already in the library through a knowledge graph.

An assistant lets users ask questions across everything they have saved, and spaced repetition quizzes help them remember material. It suits people who consume a lot of information and lose track of it.

item.title: Reclaim AI
item.description:
Reclaim is a smart scheduling assistant. You tell it your priorities, tasks with deadlines, recurring habits such as lunch or exercise, and preferred meeting hours, and it places them in your calendar. When a new meeting appears, Reclaim moves flexible items around automatically, so your calendar stays workable without constant manual rescheduling.

Several features support teams. Smart one-on-ones find times that work for both participants and adjust over time, scheduling links let others book you at times that fit your priorities, and focus time blocks protect deep work. Integrations pull tasks from tools like Asana, ClickUp, Todoist, Linear, and Jira and schedule them, and analytics show how you spend time.

item.title: Remove.bg
item.description:
Remove.bg made background removal fast and easy. You upload a photo, or drag it onto the page, and an AI model detects the foreground and returns the image with a transparent background in a few seconds. It handles people, products, animals, and cars, and it copes reasonably well with difficult edges like hair and fur. It is used for e-commerce product photos, profile pictures, ID photos, and design mockups.

The service extends beyond the website. Plugins connect it to Photoshop, Figma, and other tools, apps let you process images on a phone or desktop, and an API allows platforms to add automatic background removal at scale. Once the background is removed, you can add a solid color, a template, or another image. Bulk tools handle large catalogs. Remove.bg is owned by Canva.

item.title: Rocket
item.description:
Rocket belongs to the prompt-to-app builders. A user describes the product, and the platform generates the interface, back end logic, and database, previews it, and deploys it. Further changes are made through conversation, with the option to edit code.

It targets founders and operators who want to test an idea or build an internal tool without engineers. As with similar tools, generated apps need testing, and security and data handling deserve review before real users arrive.

item.title: Scite
item.description: Scite changes how citation counts are read. A paper with many citations may be well supported or heavily disputed, and a raw count does not tell you which. Scite analyzes the text around each citation and labels it as supporting, contrasting, or mentioning, with a snippet of the citing sentence, so you can see how others have actually used a finding. It helps researchers judge reliability and spot controversial claims.

item.title: Spellbook
item.description:
Spellbook was built to meet lawyers where they work: in Word. As you draft or review a contract, it suggests language, flags missing or risky terms, and proposes edits as tracked changes. You can ask it questions about a clause, have it compare a draft with your standard positions, or generate a first draft from a prompt, always inside the document you are working on.

Features extend to the review and negotiation steps. A library of benchmarks shows how a term compares to market standards, a playbook feature lets firms encode their preferred positions for checking contracts, and agent-style workflows can run multi-step tasks such as reviewing a set of agreements. It’s used by law firms and in-house teams, particularly for transactional work, and builds on leading language models with legal-specific prompts and data.

item.title: The SEO Agent
item.description:
The SEO Agent automates the content workflow. A user enters a site or topic, and the tool finds keywords, plans articles, and writes drafts optimized for search, with options to publish to a content management system.

It targets small sites and marketers who need regular content. The risk with automated SEO articles is quality: generic or inaccurate content rarely ranks well and can hurt a site’s credibility, so editing and original insight matter.

item.title: TheLibrarian.io
item.description:
TheLibrarian.io puts an assistant in WhatsApp. Users message it to check their email, schedule events, create tasks, and get reminders, in natural language or voice notes. It connects to services like Gmail and Google Calendar.

The appeal is simplicity: no new interface, and the chat is available anywhere. Connecting an assistant to email and calendars requires trust, so review permissions and privacy terms.

Independent information is limited. It has a free tier and paid plans. Alternatives include Notis, Poke, Lindy, Motion, and ChatGPT with connectors. TheLibrarian.io suits people who want to manage tasks through WhatsApp.

item.title: ThumbnailCreator.com
item.description:
ThumbnailCreator targets one chore. A creator describes the thumbnail they want or uploads a frame from a video, and the tool produces several thumbnail options with text, backgrounds, and subjects arranged to catch attention.

Because thumbnails strongly affect click rates, creators iterate on them often. A generator that makes variations lets them test ideas without opening a design program each time.

Independent information is limited. ThumbnailCreator has a free tier and paid plans. Alternatives include Canva, Photoroom, VidIQ and TubeBuddy thumbnail tools, Midjourney, and hiring a designer. ThumbnailCreator suits YouTubers who make many thumbnails.

item.title: v0 by Vercel
item.description: v0 started as a tool for generating user interface components from text. You described a pricing table or dashboard, and it produced React code styled with Tailwind CSS and shadcn/ui components that you could copy into a project. It has since grown into a full app builder: you can ask for pages, forms, and logic, upload a wireframe or screenshot to recreate, and watch a live preview update as you refine the result in conversation.

item.title: Voicetype AI
item.description:
Voicetype AI lets people speak instead of type. A user holds a hotkey, speaks, and the text appears in the active app, with punctuation and formatting handled automatically. It works across email, documents, chat, and code editors.

AI cleans up filler words and false starts, and supports many languages. Custom dictionaries help with names and jargon. Dictation can speed up writing for people who think out loud.

Voicetype AI has a free tier and paid plans. Independent information is limited, so check privacy and where audio is processed. Alternatives include Wispr Flow, Superwhisper, Dragon, Apple dictation, and Talon. Voicetype AI suits people who want voice typing everywhere.

item.title: Whacka
item.description:
Whacka belongs to the prompt-to-app builders. A user explains the product, and the platform generates screens, back-end logic, and data storage, previews it, and deploys it online. Changes happen through conversation.

It suits prototypes, internal tools, and tests of demand. Generated apps require testing, and security and data handling deserve review before real users or payments are involved.

Independent information is limited. Whacka has a free tier and paid plans. Alternatives include Lovable, Bolt, Replit, Base44, and Rocket. Whacka suits non-technical founders prototyping.

item.title: Wispr Flow
item.description:
Wispr Flow turns speech into polished text. A user presses a key, talks, and the cleaned-up text appears wherever the cursor is. The AI removes filler words, fixes false starts, handles punctuation, and adjusts tone to the app, so messages and documents read as if typed.

It supports many languages, custom vocabulary for names and terms, and commands for editing by voice. Writers, developers, and professionals use it to speed up emails, notes, and prompts for AI tools.

item.title: WriteABookAI
item.description:
WriteABookAI helps authors move from idea to manuscript. A writer enters a premise, and the tool proposes an outline, character profiles, and chapter drafts, which can be edited. It aims at fiction and nonfiction, with tools to track plot and consistency.

Fully AI-drafted books tend to be generic and may contain errors or contradictions, and publishing platforms and readers expect disclosure of AI use. The best outcomes come from writers who use the tool as a drafting aid and add their own voice and expertise.
